title: Add ordinal cohort stability prober and soft-halt CI gate
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Some prompt-set regressions show up only when queries are considered in an ordinal ordering (difficulty/time-of-day/sequence position). Existing cohort samplers treat prompts as unordered bags which can hide systematic drift that accumulates across ordered inputs. This PR adds a lightweight ordinal cohort stability prober and a CI 'soft-halt' gate that can pause merges when ordinal instability exceeds thresholds while offering an automated local-repair suggestion path.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a new probe implementation: probes/ordinal_prober.py. It groups prompts into ordinal buckets based on a configurable ordering function (timestamp, difficulty score, or explicit tracked position) and computes stability metrics that emphasize monotonic regressions and localized drifts.
- Introduces a CI hook: hooks/soft_halt_gate.py. Instead of a hard CI failure, the soft-halt will mark the check required and present structured diagnostics plus a recommended minimal repair (reweighting prompts, minor prompt edits or temporary canary rollback suggestions).
- Integrates with the eval runner: cli.py gains --ordinal-probe, the orchestration pipeline reports new metrics (ordinal_stability_index, localized_regression_hotspots).
- Adds unit and integration tests under tests/ordinal_prober_test.py and tests/ci_soft_halt_integration.py.
- Documentation: docs/ordinal-cohort.md describing the algorithm, tuning knobs, and recommended thresholds for typical Redwood workloads.

Design notes and constraints:
- The ordinal prober is intentionally inexpensive: it samples streams and maintains exponentially weighted counters per bucket to keep memory bounded for long prompt histories.
- Stability score is a composite of monotonicity loss (detects drift trends), bucket-wise A/B delta (detects localized spikes), and a time-decay factor to prioritize recent regressions.
- The soft-halt gate is advisory by default for non-blocking branches; team and linear ticket ENG-4278 propose enabling a hard-block for release branches after N weeks of opt-in.

Risk/compatibility:
- Feature gates added so existing CI flows are unaffected unless the --ordinal-probe flag or the soft-halt check is enabled in repo config.
- No changes to runtime inference code.

Related: this complements existing cohort and semantic-prober work (see ENG-3312, ENG-4120).

review_thread:
Evan Brooks: This looks promising — can you explain the rationale for the EWMA decay constants? I worry about sensitivity on low-volume prompt-sets.

Maya Chen: Good call. Default decay is conservative (0.01) and made configurable. I added a unit test that simulates low-volume buckets and adjusted thresholds to avoid false positives (see tests/ordinal_prober_test.py).

Sana Iqbal: CI integration is clever, but we should make the soft-halt visible to oncall dashboards. Can the diagnostics payload include cohort anchor samples and top-5 lexically different examples?

Maya Chen: Added ordinal_reporter which attaches anchor samples and top diffs to the gate payload. Also wired a logging hook to the eval dashboard ingestion.

Diego Marquez: Performance: the runner now does per-request sampling; have you measured end-to-end added latency?

Maya Chen: Benchmarked on benchmark-lab with production-like trace (1000 req/s) — adding ordinal sampling at 5% sampling rate adds ~0.4ms p50 and ~1.2ms p95. Results included in the PR description and tests. I added a sampler rate config to tune cost.

Evan Brooks: Left a small style nit in ordinal_prober compute_buckets; otherwise approving after tests are green.

Maya Chen: Addressed nit and pushed fix.

release_notes: Add an experimental ordinal cohort stability prober and a configurable soft-halt CI gate to detect ordering-sensitive regressions. Opt-in via --ordinal-probe or CI config. Includes reporter payloads for diagnostics and example thresholds in docs/ordinal-cohort.md.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: feature is off by default and must be enabled per-repo. Next steps suggested in ENG-4278: 1) pilot on a few high-volume prompt-sets, 2) iterate on default decay and threshold heuristics, 3) evaluate candidate autopatch rules for the local-repair suggestions.
